source:
Ravi: The night shift should go back to eight hours. Twelve-hour shifts are why the error count doubled since spring.
Suki: The error count doubled because we switched to the new labeling system in May, the same month the shifts changed. The shift length is a coincidence.
Ravi: The errors cluster in the last three hours of each shift. That is a fatigue pattern, not a software pattern.
Suki: The last three hours are also when the label printer queue backs up. You are reading fatigue into a bottleneck.

extraction.mainQuestion: What caused the night-shift error count to double since spring?

positions.label: Twelve-hour shifts cause the errors
positions.thesis: Errors doubled because twelve-hour shifts produce fatigue, so the night shift should return to eight hours.
positions.steelman: Errors cluster in the final three hours of every shift, which is the signature of fatigue rather than of a system change.

groundingQuotes.quote: Twelve-hour shifts are why the error count doubled since spring.
Fatigue is the only explanation that fits the data we have collected.
Every study of shift length says the same thing.

positions.label: The new labeling system causes the errors
positions.thesis: Errors doubled because the labeling system changed in May, and the late-shift clustering matches the printer queue backing up.
positions.steelman: Two changes happened in the same month; the one with a documented bottleneck at exactly the hours where errors cluster is the software, not the schedule.

groundingQuotes.quote: The labeling rollout notes show a spike in reprints from day one.
We measured the queue and it peaks at hour nine.
Nobody on the day shift saw any change in error rate.

claims.statement: Errors cluster in the last three hours of each shift.

resolution.condition: Error timestamps by hour of shift.

groundingQuotes.quote: The errors cluster in the last three hours of each shift.

claims.statement: The label printer queue backs up in the same late-shift hours where errors cluster.

resolution.condition: Printer queue logs by hour compared with error timestamps.

groundingQuotes.quote: The last three hours are also when the label printer queue backs up.

disagreementCandidates.question: Are the late-shift errors caused by fatigue or by the label printer bottleneck?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Both accept the late-shift clustering; Ravi reads it as fatigue from twelve-hour shifts, Suki as the printer queue from the May labeling change.

participantStances.stance: Fatigue; the clustering is the signature.
The printer queue; same hours, different cause.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Compare error timing with printer queue logs and with shift length on days the queue was clear.

caveats: This fixture deliberately supplies position quotes that do not appear in the source, standing in for a model that invented supporting sentences. Every invented quote must be dropped and the diagnosis downgraded rather than repaired.
